citations.title: Community-Integrated Living Arrangements Licensure and Certification Act
citations.requirement: Statutory basis for CILA agency licensure and site certification. A CILA is a site where 8 or fewer individuals with a developmental disability live under agency supervision.

citations.title: Licensure of community developmental services agencies
citations.requirement: Licensure requirements and fees. Application fee is capped at $200. Rule 115.410(b) points to Section 4(d) for the nonrefundable licensure and renewal fee. Agencies certify compliance with Section 4 in the application.

citations.title: Purpose
citations.requirement: Sets uniform direction for licensure and operation of CILA agencies.

citations.title: Definitions
citations.requirement: Defines the terms the manual must use. Key definitions: CILA (8 or fewer), Continuous supervision or support (staff physically on-site all hours individuals are present unless the Personal Plan and Implementation Strategy say otherwise), Critical Incidents, DSP, Implementation Strategy, Informed consent, Coercion, Aversive procedures, Restraint, Governing body, Authorized CILA agency representative, Independent Monitor and Receiver, Community integration, Authorized electronic monitoring.

citations.title: Description
citations.requirement: CILA settings and services must support integration and full community access, control of personal resources, privacy, dignity and respect, and freedom from coercion and restraint (except as 115.245 allows). They must optimize individual initiative and autonomy and be physically accessible, with communal areas meeting ADA standards. Agencies must follow person-centered planning rules (42 CFR 441.301(c)(1)-(3), 59 Ill. Adm. Code 120, 115.230). The CILA rate excludes day programs, which are billed separately. Informed consent to participate in a CILA must be documented. Subsection letters to be pinned from the official text.

citations.title: Respite Services for Persons with a Developmental Disability
citations.requirement: Before respite, the agency requires a physician statement that the individual has no contagious disease. It also documents that the individual will not jeopardize the health or safety of others in the home. Respite longer than two weeks needs Department approval before the initial two weeks end, and only in emergencies.

citations.title: Criteria for Participation of Individuals
citations.requirement: Individuals must be at least 18 with a developmental disability and need CILA services and a supervised living arrangement. Agencies may request an age waiver for individuals at least 17.5. An agency's lack of capacity for a particular disability does not make the individual ineligible. No otherwise qualified individual may be denied placement solely on diagnosis. Admission policies must be in writing and available for review (subsection to be pinned).

citations.title: Individuals Requiring Additional Services and Support
citations.requirement: Process for team requests for additional staff resources or supports. The Department responds as soon as possible and no later than ten business days after receipt. Need for non-base support hours is professionally reviewed at least annually and reported to the Department. Subsection letters to be pinned.

citations.title: Criteria for Termination from a CILA Agency
citations.requirement: Sets the criteria under which services may be terminated. 115.250 says individuals may remain in a CILA unless they voluntarily withdraw or meet these criteria. Section text was NOT retrieved; pull it verbatim before finalizing.

citations.title: Services and Supports
citations.requirement: The agency maintains a Provider Support Team for each individual. The team includes a QIDP and a DSP, plus a nurse or other professionals as needed. The team is responsible for service functions in the Personal Plan areas the agency covers and for developing the Implementation Strategy. It provides care and supervision based on assessed needs, helps the person take part in community supports, and is available 24 hours. It advocates, helps the person keep safety and comforts, and provides counseling and crisis problem-solving. It helps with ADLs and assistive devices and helps individuals access medication information, including observing and reporting effects and side effects. It supports the individual's right to sexual health and freedom from sexual exploitation, including a decision-making capacity assessment for consent to sexual activity.

citations.title: Assessments
citations.requirement: Individual assessments inform the Personal Plan and Implementation Strategy. Rule text mentions an annual Department web-based health risk screening tool, with a paper-completion request allowed with justification. The section text and subsection number were NOT confirmed; verify before citing the subsection.

citations.title: Person-Centered Planning
citations.requirement: Agencies comply with 42 CFR 441.301(c)(1)-(3) and 59 Ill. Adm. Code 120. Within 20 calendar days of the provider's dated signature on the Personal Plan, the agency develops an Implementation Strategy on Form IL462-4470. The strategy is based on the Personal Plan and assessments, with the individual and guardian taking part (ISC as necessary). It is signed by the individual and guardian and addresses the outcomes the agency agreed to support. The individual and guardian get a copy of the strategy and its updates, and it becomes part of the record. At least monthly the QIDP reviews the strategy and documents the review. A CILA rate determination packet for intermittent supports is submitted by the ISC with the CILA agency. Individuals needing continuous supervision may stay alone or access the community independently only under specified circumstances. The provider support team must assess this, and it must be based on need and preference, not staff convenience. The strategy states the time periods and locations/time frames involved.

citations.title: Medical Services and Medications
citations.requirement: When agency employees provide medical services or medications, or supervise their administration, the agency certifies this is done under the Mental Health and DD Administrative Act and 59 Ill. Adm. Code 116. A licensed physician (MD/DO) is responsible for medical services, including prescribing. A physician examines the individual before psychotropics start. AIMS screening is done at least every six months for individuals on psychotropics. A physician reviews medications and sees the individual at least every six months, more often if a psychiatrist requires.

citations.title: Restraints
citations.requirement: Prone, supine and mechanical restraint are prohibited. Any use must be reported in CIRAS and to the Office of the Inspector General. Other restraint is allowed only if every condition is met. There must be an immediate threat of serious physical harm, with less restrictive measures proven ineffective. Restraint must be a modification in the Personal Plan, approved by the individual or guardian and the Provider Support Team, and in the behavior strategy. It needs Behavior Management/Human Rights Committee approval and a plan to reduce and eliminate it. Staff must be trained in the specific restraint, and the agency must document no medical or psychological contraindication. Staff involved in restraint not in the Personal Plan may be required to complete remediation training. The agency keeps a copy of its restraint policy.

citations.title: Individual Rights and Confidentiality
citations.requirement: The agency shares and explains the current Rights of Individuals form (IL 462-1201) at entry and annually. Rights are protected under Chapter II of the Mental Health and DD Code, and seclusion is not permitted. Individuals have the right to remain in the CILA unless they withdraw or meet 115.215 criteria. They may contact the Guardianship and Advocacy Commission, Equip for Equality, the Department's OIG, the Department and the agency's human rights committee. Staff offer help and give each individual the address and telephone number of GAC, OIG, the Department and Equip for Equality. Individuals have the right to be free from abuse, neglect, exploitation, coercion and restraint. Seclusion, time-out and aversive procedures are prohibited. Individuals may use private physicians and professionals of their choice, documented in the plan.

citations.title: Environmental Management of Living Arrangements
citations.requirement: Copies of local and State health, sanitation and environment inspections are maintained. The agency keeps a disaster preparedness plan covering disasters and public health crises, reviewed annually. Fire and disaster training records are available to DDD and BALC at the site, and corrective actions for drill or inspection deficiencies are recorded. Staff and individuals know how to react to fire, severe weather, missing persons, psychiatric and medical emergencies, poison control and deaths. Staff are trained in the location of extinguishers, first aid kits and evacuation routes. An operational telephone is accessible, with a posted list of the site phone number and nearest poison control center. Evacuation drills include actual evacuation to safe areas. At least one approved fire extinguisher has an annual inspection tag. Red Cross-standard first aid kits are checked quarterly and restocked. New individuals are trained within 30 days of moving in. Residences must comply with local building codes. Subsection numbers beyond (c)(8) to be pinned from the official text.

citations.title: Geographic Location of Community-Integrated Living Arrangements
citations.requirement: Siting rules for HCBS settings. New provider-owned or controlled sites may not be adjacent to, across from, diagonal to or behind another waiver-funded residential or day site of the same provider unless a waiver is granted. They may not be in a building that provides inpatient institutional treatment. No more than 25% of units in a building may be Department-funded CILAs owned or controlled by CILA providers. Waiver requests are filed before leasing, buying or taking possession.

citations.title: Administrative Requirements
citations.requirement: (a) Corporate, association or local-government providers have a governing body with authority over operations. Providers must have a way to get input from individuals, guardians and representatives to the governing body. (b) Employees are licensed or certified as Illinois law requires. The agency may not employ anyone (including contractors, volunteers and practitioners) until it has checked the DPH Health Care Worker Registry and the DCFS State Central Register/CANTS. It must also have received the results of the applicable registry or list, and the inquiry may not occur more than 30 calendar days before the first day of employment. Checks are repeated on a schedule that completes them every 365 days. The agency complies with the Health Care Worker Background Check Act. (d) DSPs and anyone with direct care responsibility demonstrate competence in the listed training areas (A)-(M) as part of orientation, with enough trained staff to cover absences. (e) Volunteer training applies. The section also requires the agency to notify the individual's guardian or parent of an abuse/neglect allegation within 24 hours of receiving it. Each agency must have and use a process for reporting and handling complaints. Exact paragraph letters to be pinned.

citations.title: Application for Waiver of the Prohibition Against Employment
citations.requirement: Provides the process for applying for a waiver of the prohibition against employment (Health Care Worker Background Check Act). Only the section title was retrieved; pull the text before writing the procedure.

citations.title: Monitoring and Evaluation
citations.requirement: Agency monitoring and evaluation obligations. Only the section title was retrieved; pull the text before writing the QI procedure.

citations.title: Monitors and Receiverships
citations.requirement: New section in the 2024 Rule 115 amendments. Substantive triggers and roles come from the 115.120 definitions of Independent Monitor and Receiver. The section text itself was not retrieved.

citations.title: License Application
citations.requirement: New-provider requirements must be completed within one year of requesting an application. The application certifies compliance with Section 4 of the Act, the Confidentiality Act, Part 115, 59 Ill. Adm. Code 120 and 42 CFR 441.301(c)(1)-(4). Settings must not be of the type in 42 CFR 441.301(c)(5)(v), and provider-owned or controlled sites must meet (c)(4)(vi)(A)-(E). The application requires agency policies and procedures, an organizational chart, staffing patterns and staff qualifications. The nonrefundable fee follows Section 4(d) of the Act. The renewal application is due at least 120 days before expiration after Department notice. BALC and DDD must be notified of any ownership change within 60 business days. The agency must be operational within 18 months or the application is treated as abandoned.

citations.title: 24-Hour Service
citations.requirement: 24-hour service requirement. It sits in Subpart E (Host Family Living Arrangements), so cite it only for host family settings. For shift-staff homes rely on the continuous supervision definition in 115.120 and the Personal Plan/Implementation Strategy.

citations.title: Definitions (abuse, neglect, financial exploitation) - OIG Rule 50
citations.requirement: 115.120 adopts the Part 50.10 definitions of abuse and financial exploitation, and critical incidents include abuse, neglect and exploitation as defined in Part 50. Only the incorporation by reference was verified, not the Part 50 text itself. Reporting steps and timelines in Part 50 were NOT retrieved.

citations.title: Referenced in 115.240 (medication administration)
citations.requirement: 115.240 requires certification that medications are provided or supervised in line with the Administrative Act and Part 116. The Part 116 title and text were NOT retrieved; confirm the title and requirements before citing.

citations.title: Person-Centered Planning
citations.requirement: HCBS waiver participants, guardians, ISC agencies and provider agencies comply with person-centered planning requirements. Providers develop an Implementation Strategy within 20 calendar days of signing the Personal Plan.

citations.title: Mental Health and Developmental Disabilities Confidentiality Act
citations.requirement: Governs confidentiality of records and communications. Rule 115 requires agencies to certify compliance, and informed consent includes consent for releases of information. Act text was not retrieved; only its incorporation by Part 115.

citations.title: Mental Health and Developmental Disabilities Code - rights
citations.requirement: 115.250 requires individual rights to be protected under Chapter II of the Code, except that seclusion is not permitted.

citations.title: Health Care Worker Background Check Act
citations.requirement: Part 115 implements this Act (per its authority note), and 115.320(b) requires compliance. The Act text was not retrieved.

citations.title: Authorized Electronic Monitoring in Community-Integrated Living Arrangements and Developmental Disability Facilities Act
citations.requirement: 115.120 defines authorized electronic monitoring and electronic monitoring devices by reference to this Act. Monitoring is placement of a device in an individual's room under the Act. Act text was not retrieved.

citations.cite: IDHS New Provider Guidance - Steps for CILA
citations.title: New Provider Guidance - Steps for CILA
citations.requirement: Criminal background check before hire and annually. Illinois State Police fingerprint check reported to the Health Care Worker Registry. Staff trained as DSP (DD Aide) or completing training before working alone, with completion reported to HCWR. Anyone giving direct care more than 20% of the time is trained as a DSP. First aid/CPR and OIG Rule 50 abuse/neglect training renew every two years. RN with unencumbered Illinois license who completes DHS/DDD RN trainer webinars. BALC unannounced visit within one year of first admission, site visit within six months, then permanent license.

citations.title: Contents of request for a waiver - person-centered planning and HCBS settings
citations.requirement: Rule 115.410(a)(2) requires CILAs serving waiver participants to meet person-centered planning and settings requirements in (c)(1)-(4). Settings may not be of the type in (c)(5)(v), and provider-owned or controlled sites must meet (c)(4)(vi)(A)-(E).

citations.cite: Medicaid HCBS Waiver for Adults with Developmental Disabilities (IL.0350.R05.04)
citations.title: 1915(c) waiver in effect January 1, 2026
citations.requirement: Waiver under which CILA services are paid. HFS is the Medicaid agency and IDHS-DDD is the operating agency.

citations.title: Person-Centered Planning Process - IDHS
citations.requirement: Provider signature page is due back to the ISC within 10 calendar days of receiving the Personal Plan. The Implementation Strategy is due within 20 calendar days of the QIDP signing the Provider Signature Page.

citations.cite: IDHS Person Centered Planning Policy and Guidelines for DD Waiver Services
citations.title: Person Centered Planning Policy and Guidelines
citations.requirement: Providers give the individual/guardian and ISC a copy of the Implementation Strategy. The individual or guardian signs it, and the guidance says the ISC does not sign or approve it. Providers must make sure all billed services are identified in the Personal Plan and tell the ISC if a service change is needed.

citations.cite: IDHS DDD Electronic Visit Verification (EVV) Policy
citations.title: Electronic Visit Verification (EVV) Policy
citations.requirement: EVV for IMPACT-enrolled providers billing personal care or home health care services. From April 1, 2026, providers must keep quarterly EVV compliance above 75%. Whether 60D/61H CILA claims are covered is unverified; confirm with DDD.

citations.title: IMPACT Provider Enrollment
citations.requirement: IMPACT is the Medicaid enrollment and reimbursement system. Enrollment must be completed before federal reimbursement.

citations.title: January 1, 2024 Wage/Rate Increase
citations.requirement: CILA provider agencies certify that wage increases are passed through to direct care staff.

citations.cite: IDHS Independent Service Coordination (ISC) Manual, Section 8.2
citations.title: Person Centered Planning - The Discovery Process
citations.requirement: The ISC has 30 calendar days after the person begins DDD Waiver services to complete Discovery and develop the Personal Plan. The ISC submits the Crisis Transition Plan and Funding Request for people in crisis (homelessness, abuse or neglect).

citations.title: Standards and Licensure Requirements for Community-Integrated Living Arrangements
citations.requirement: Part-level cite, used where a rule paragraph was seen but its exact section/subsection was not confirmed. That includes the required record contents (written informed consent to participate, prior service history, Personal Plan), admission policies in writing, life-safety compliance, current Personal Plans/Implementation Strategies kept at the residence, and surveys at renewal and for complaints. Pin the exact section from the official text before finalizing. Amended effective 5/31/2023 (47 Ill. Reg. 8485).

policies.title: Governing Body Authority and Responsibilities
state_specifics: The governing body holds authority and responsibility for the organization, management, control and operation of the CILA agency and all programs, services, facilities and residences.
It appoints the Authorized CILA Agency Representative, who receives critical-incident trends (see CI-01).
It approves the policy manual, the QA plan (QA-01) and the annual review of rights-restricting policies.
Sole-proprietor or owner-operated agencies document who exercises these functions. The rule text covers corporations, associations and local governments.

policies.title: Input from Individuals, Guardians and Representatives to the Governing Body
state_specifics: The policy states the mechanism that carries input from individuals served, guardians and representatives to the governing body (e.g., a standing agenda item, annual survey, or seat on the board or HRC).
Input and the governing body's response are logged and kept for BALC review.
Offer accessible formats and supports so individuals can take part.

policies.title: Organization, Organizational Chart, Staffing Patterns, Qualifications and Policy Manual Control
state_specifics: The license application requires agency policies and procedures, an organizational chart, staffing patterns and staff qualifications.
Use Part 115 defined terms (Personal Plan, Implementation Strategy, DSP, QIDP, continuous supervision).
Version-control the manual with an annual review. The effective date and approver are recorded.
Confirm current QIDP, administrator and director qualifications with BALC before naming anyone.

policies.title: Staff Licensure and Certification; Supervision of Paraprofessional, Contractual and Volunteer Workers
state_specifics: Employees must hold the licenses or certifications Illinois law requires, and the credential is verified at hire. RN licenses are verified on the IDFPR site.
Paraprofessional, non-professional contractual workers and volunteers in direct service are supervised by professional employees.
Keep a roster showing each non-professional worker's supervising professional.

policies.title: Pre-Employment and Annual Registry Checks
state_specifics: Before any employment, including contractors, volunteers and practitioners with care responsibility: DPH Health Care Worker Registry, DCFS State Central Register/CANTS, Illinois Sex Offender Registry and HFS Sanctions List.
Results must be received before the first day of employment. The inquiry may not be dated more than 30 calendar days before the first day.
Registry findings of abuse, egregious neglect, a sex offense or a disqualifying conviction with no waiver bar employment. If the HFS Sanctions List shows an exclusion, confirm status with HFS OIG.
Repeat all four checks annually so each person is checked every 365 days: on the hire anniversary, at the performance-evaluation date, or on a written schedule.
A person newly placed on a registry or list is terminated. Staff also receive a criminal background check before hire and annually.

policies.title: Health Care Worker Background Check Act Compliance and Waivers
state_specifics: The agency complies with 225 ILCS 46 and never knowingly hires or retains a person outside the Act.
A person on the Health Care Worker Registry may request a waiver on the DPH-prescribed form.
A waiver of a CANTS indication is requested under Department-published guidelines.
115.321 (waiver of the prohibition against employment): pull the verbatim text before finalizing the procedure.

policies.title: Staffing Patterns, Continuous Supervision and Awake Overnight Staff
state_specifics: Continuous supervision or support means staff are physically on-site all hours individuals are present, unless the Personal Plan and Implementation Strategy say otherwise.
No licensure ratio was found in Part 115. Staffing levels come from each individual's Personal Plan and the DDD rate letter, so do not state a ratio as a rule.
Awake overnight status is a DDD rate-funding definition. Record each home's overnight model in the Implementation Strategy.

Individuals needing continuous supervision may be alone or in the community independently only as 115.230 allows, based on need and preference and not staff convenience. 115.580 applies to host family settings only.

policies.title: Personnel Records and Employee Health and TB Screening
state_specifics: Each file holds the credential verification, dated registry results, annual recheck dates, training and competence documentation, and the DSP/First Aid/CPR/OIG Rule 50 expiry dates.
Training must be available to BALC and DDD for review.
No TB-screening rule was retrieved from Part 115. Confirm current IDPH and BALC requirements before setting the screening schedule.
Employee medical information is kept in a file separate from the personnel file.

policies.title: Staff Conduct and Professional Boundaries
state_specifics: Staff are prohibited from abuse, neglect, exploitation, coercion, aversive procedures and misuse of individuals' funds or property.
Staff must report suspected abuse, neglect or exploitation under GPR-05.
Staff conduct involving gifts, loans, social media, dating or sexual contact with individuals is addressed, consistent with the sexual-exploitation protections in 115.220.
Violations lead to discipline and, where Part 50 or registry rules apply, reporting.

policies.title: Cumulative Case Records, Personal Plan and Implementation Strategy
state_specifics: A cumulative case record with a Personal Plan and Implementation Strategy is maintained for each individual.
Current Personal Plans and Implementation Strategies are kept at the residence.
Implementation Strategy is on Form IL462-4470 (see PCS-01 for timelines).

policies.title: Human Rights Committee
state_specifics: At least 5 members. At least one is a person served and/or a family member or guardian. At least one-third are not former employees, former individuals or guardians, vendors, or employees of other CILA/DD providers.
Members are not shared with the Behavior Management Committee, except a physician, APRN, RN, or nurse practitioner/physician assistant.
Annual review of policies that could restrict rights. Review of any practice restricting a specific individual's rights at least every six months.
Informs the agency of rights complaints, deficiencies and corrective actions, and includes individuals, guardians and natural supports in meetings about their services.
Minutes record attendance, each individual's decision, justification and intended outcome. When a restrictive intervention is approved, the next review date is recorded.

policies.title: Behavior Management Committee and Positive Behavior Support
state_specifics: Required when the program uses behavioral interventions under 115.214. At least 5 members.

Approves behavior interventions before use and reviews them at least every six months. Reviews all behavior strategies at least annually and determines whether a rights restriction exists. Plans with a restriction also go to the Human Rights Committee.

Members include persons qualified to evaluate interventions. A licensed professional qualified to evaluate drug use is a member when drugs manage behavior. At least one member is from outside the agency.
Minutes record attendance and decisions. The committee seeks input from individuals, guardians and natural supports.
Behavior strategies emphasize positive supports and never use seclusion, time-out or aversive procedures.

policies.title: Restraint, Seclusion, Time-Out and Aversive Procedures
state_specifics: Prone, supine and mechanical restraint are prohibited. Any use is reported in CIRAS and to the DHS Office of the Inspector General.

Other restraint only with an immediate threat of serious physical harm, less restrictive measures proven ineffective, and a Personal Plan modification approved by the individual or guardian and the Provider Support Team.

It also requires Behavior Management/Human Rights Committee approval, a plan to reduce and eliminate it, staff trained in the specific restraint, and documented absence of medical or psychological contraindication.
Seclusion, time-out and aversive procedures are prohibited.
Staff involved in restraint not in the Personal Plan may be required to complete remediation training. The agency keeps its restraint policy on file.

policies.title: Abuse, Neglect and Exploitation Prevention, Reporting and Handling Process
state_specifics: The agency has and uses a process for reporting and handling abuse, neglect and exploitation under applicable standards, regulations and laws (59 Ill. Adm. Code 50 definitions).
Notify the individual allegedly abused, neglected or exploited, and their guardian or parent, within 24 hours after receiving the allegation.
Report to OIG within 4 hours of discovery (see CI-02).
Staff complete OIG Rule 50 training at orientation and every two years.

policies.title: Rights Complaints and Grievances
state_specifics: The agency has and uses a process for reporting and handling complaints about individual rights, in addition to abuse/neglect reporting.
Share and explain the Rights of Individuals form (IL 462-1201) with the individual and/or guardian at entry and annually.
Give each person the address and phone of the Guardianship and Advocacy Commission, DHS OIG, DHS and Equip for Equality, and offer help contacting them.
Rights complaints go to the Human Rights Committee (GPR-02). No retaliation.

policies.title: Nondiscrimination, Admission Policies and Procedures, Referral and Respite
state_specifics: No discrimination in admission or services on race, color, sex, religion (creed), gender identity, gender expression, age, national origin (ancestry), ethnicity, disability, marital status, sexual orientation or military status.
Admission policies and procedures are in writing and available for review.

Eligibility: at least 18 (age waiver request possible at 17.5+) with a developmental disability, needing CILA services and a supervised living arrangement. No otherwise qualified person is denied solely on diagnosis, and lack of capacity for a disability does not make a person ineligible.

Respite: a physician statement of no contagious disease, plus documentation that the person will not jeopardize others' health or safety. Respite over two weeks needs Department approval before the first two weeks end, and only in emergencies.
Referrals come through ISC agencies. Crisis transitions follow the ISC Crisis Transition Plan and Funding Request.

policies.title: Life Safety, Code Compliance, Residential Environment and Siting
state_specifics: All program facilities comply with State licensure requirements and local ordinances on fire, building, zoning, sanitation, health and safety.
BALC inspects a new agency-owned or leased site before occupancy. OSFM fire clearance is part of the process.

Siting: no adjacent, across, diagonal or behind sites of the same provider without a waiver, filed before leasing, buying or taking possession. No site in a building giving inpatient institutional treatment. Department-funded provider-controlled CILAs may be no more than 25% of units in a building.
Communal areas meet ADA standards. Keep copies of local and State health, sanitation and environment inspections at the site.

policies.title: Visits by Protection and Advocacy Groups
state_specifics: Department-authorized individual protection and advocacy interest groups may visit provider-owned or controlled living arrangements, with the consent of the individual or guardian.
Staff record the visit and the consent, and never refuse or discourage a visit the individual has agreed to.
Respect each person's privacy during the visit.

policies.title: Remote Monitoring and Supports; Authorized Electronic Monitoring
state_specifics: Applies only if the agency offers remote monitoring and supports under 305 ILCS 5/12-21.21, as DDD determines. Otherwise the policy states the agency does not offer it.
Each use rests on an assessment that identifies the risks bearing on whether remote supports suit the individual.
Authorized electronic monitoring (a device in an individual's room) follows 210 ILCS 165, not this process. Document consent and privacy protections.
Any monitoring is a Personal Plan modification where it restricts privacy, with HRC review (GPR-02).

policies.title: Direct Support Professional Orientation, Competency, Written Training Plan and Ongoing Development
state_specifics: DSPs and others with direct care responsibility (including paraprofessionals, contractual workers and volunteers) demonstrate competence in the (d)(1) training areas during orientation.

Staff with no direct-service experience receive training and demonstrate competence before unsupervised responsibility, unless trained employees are on site for on-the-job training. Enough staff are trained to cover absences.
Anyone giving direct care more than 20% of the time is trained as a DSP. First aid/CPR and OIG Rule 50 training renew every two years.
Written training plan lists the training offered, the methods, and how competency is determined. An employee development plan covers ongoing training after orientation.
All training is documented and readily available to BALC and DDD. DDD approves the agency's DSP and QIDP training programs after IMPACT enrollment.

policies.title: CPR, First Aid, Choking Response, Safety, Disaster, Fire and Hot Water Temperature Training
state_specifics: CPR, back blows/abdominal thrusts and first aid. Renew every two years.
Safety and disaster procedures, public health emergencies, fire procedures and use of fire extinguishers.
Techniques for monitoring and regulating hot water temperature before and during use for hand-washing, hair-washing, bathing and showering. Water should be between 100 and 110 degrees.
New individuals are trained on emergency procedures within 30 days of moving in (115.300).

policies.title: Habilitation, Personal Plan, Implementation Strategy, Documentation and Disability-Specific Training
state_specifics: Concepts of habilitation and rehabilitation, including behavior intervention and management, age appropriateness and psycho-social rehabilitation, as the individuals served need.
Purpose and content of the Personal Plan. Development and implementation of an Implementation Strategy (IL462-4470).
Documentation and recordkeeping for the Personal Plan and Implementation Strategy.
Other training specific to the type of disability or treatment techniques used for individuals living in the CILA, geared to carrying out Personal Plan outcomes.

policies.title: Abuse, Neglect, Exploitation, Coercion, Critical Incident, Rights and Confidentiality Training
state_specifics: Abuse, neglect, exploitation, coercion and critical incident prevention, handling and reporting to the DHS OIG under 59 Ill. Adm. Code 50.
Individual rights under 115.250 and confidentiality under the Mental Health and Developmental Disabilities Confidentiality Act (740 ILCS 110).
OIG Rule 50 training renews every two years.
Competence is shown by test, observation or scenario and recorded in the personnel file.

policies.title: Medication and AIMS Training; Nurse-Trainer Certification of Direct Care Staff
state_specifics: Type, dosage, characteristics, effects and side effects of prescribed medications, with enough trained staff to cover expected and unexpected absences.
Observation with the AIMS (Abnormal Involuntary Movement Skills) for tardive dyskinesia.

Before supervising self-administration or administering medication, unlicensed direct care staff meet 59 Ill. Adm. Code 116.40(c), including a Department-approved program taught by a CILA agency Nurse-Trainer.
Staff are re-evaluated by a Nurse-Trainer at least annually, or sooner at the RN's discretion, with retraining as needed.
The Nurse-Trainer RN holds an unencumbered Illinois license and completes the DHS/DDD RN trainer webinars. Pull Part 116 text and the current course requirements before finalizing.

policies.title: Volunteer Orientation, Training and Supervision
state_specifics: Orientation and training specific to the volunteer's duties, with supervision as necessary.
Volunteers with responsibility for the care of individuals complete and demonstrate competency in all (d) training areas.
Volunteers are registry-checked before starting (STF-02) and are never left unsupervised with individuals unless trained and checked.
Track volunteer hours and training in a volunteer file.

policies.title: Written Quality Assurance Plan, Data Review and Mortality Review
state_specifics: A written QA plan and ongoing activities review and evaluate services to individuals and program operation, and resolve identified problems.
The QA program is the basis for determining that individuals receive appropriate services consistent with their Personal Plans and Implementation Strategies.
Inputs: critical incident trends, rights complaints, medication errors, record audits, individual and guardian feedback and death reviews.
Results go to the governing body (GOV-01). 115.325 (Monitoring and Evaluation): pull the verbatim text before finalizing.

policies.title: Correction of Deficiencies and Withdrawal of CILA Certification
state_specifics: If a certified CILA stops meeting standards, correct the deficiencies within 30 days.
If they cannot be corrected in 30 days, withdraw certification of that CILA program and notify the Department.
The agency stays responsible for affected individuals until they have transitioned to other settings.
Record each corrective action and its completion date. Use it for mock inspections ahead of BALC visits.

policies.title: Critical Incident Handling, Investigation, Tracking and Analysis
state_specifics: Written procedures for handling, investigating, reporting, tracking and analyzing critical incidents through the management structure, up to and including the Authorized CILA Agency Representative.
Employees demonstrate knowledge of the procedures and follow them.
Critical incident categories follow the 115.120 definition, which includes abuse, neglect and exploitation as defined in Part 50.
Trend analysis feeds the QA plan (QA-01) and the Human Rights Committee.

policies.title: Reporting to Law Enforcement, DHS OIG and CIRAS
state_specifics: Report any incident subject to the Criminal Code of 2012 (720 ILCS 5) to local law enforcement within 24 hours of occurrence.
Report suspected abuse, neglect or exploitation to the DHS Office of Inspector General within 4 hours of discovery. Post the current OIG hotline number at each site and confirm it before printing.
Report all other critical incidents electronically to DDD through CIRAS. Incidents are those listed under Critical Incidents in 115.120.
Notify the guardian or parent of an abuse/neglect allegation within 24 hours (GPR-05).
Any restraint use is reported in CIRAS and to OIG.

policies.title: Missing Person and Elopement
state_specifics: Staff and individuals are trained on how to react to a missing person (115.300).
Each individual's risk and supervision level is set in the Personal Plan and Implementation Strategy. Independent time follows 115.230.
Immediate search, then law enforcement notice and guardian notice. Report to CIRAS as a critical incident and to OIG if neglect is suspected.
Keep a current photo and description in each record.

policies.title: Death of an Individual
state_specifics: Staff are trained on how to respond to a death (115.300).
Call 911 and begin CPR unless a valid directive says otherwise. Then notify the guardian or emergency contact and the physician.
Report the death in CIRAS and notify OIG when abuse or neglect is suspected. Preserve the scene and records.
Complete a mortality review feeding the QA plan (QA-01).

policies.title: Record Confidentiality and Safekeeping
state_specifics: Confidentiality follows the Mental Health and Developmental Disabilities Confidentiality Act (740 ILCS 110).
Safeguard all records against loss or destruction with locked storage and access-controlled electronic systems.
Releases of information require valid consent. A copy of each authorization is kept in the record.
Staff receive confidentiality training at orientation.

policies.title: Chronological Record Standards and Electronic Signatures
state_specifics: A chronological record for each individual is accessible at the program site. Entries are legible, dated and signed with title. Corrections are initialed and the original stays legible. Symbols and abbreviations use an agency-wide legend.

Electronic signatures need an adopted policy, a unique identifier from a confidential access code, written confidentiality and sole-user certifications, and periodic monitoring with corrective action.

Verification: required fields are completed, corrections are made by separate authenticated entries, the user can verify the document, and records are sampled periodically. Each generated report is separately authenticated.

policies.title: Record Contents at Entry and During Service
state_specifics: At entry: identifying information, guardianship order, guardian or emergency contact, language and preferred communication mode, medications, reactions and allergies, physical and dental exams and medical history, consent to emergency medical services, and releases of information.

During service: written informed consent to participate in a CILA, prior service history, Personal Plan and Implementation Strategy, assessments and reassessments, approvals for special procedures and their results, and monthly QIDP-signed and dated progress documentation.
Keep all items updated as necessary.
Assessments follow 115.225. Verify the subsection against the official text.

policies.title: Record Retention, Access and Required Reports to the State
state_specifics: Record retention period: confirm with BALC/DDD and the waiver document before setting it. No period was verified here.
Records are available to BALC and DDD on request.

Required reports: CIRAS incidents, OIG reports, restraint reports, ownership change notice within 60 business days, renewal application at least 120 days before expiry, and the annual rights-restriction and health-risk reviews.
Keep a calendar of recurring State report due dates.

policies.title: Department Contractual and Financial Requirements, Medicaid Billing and Documentation, EVV and Wage Pass-Through
state_specifics: The agency complies with Department rules on its contractual and financial relationship with the Department.
Bill only services identified in the Personal Plan, and notify the ISC if a service change is needed.
Enrollment and billing run through IMPACT, and enrollment must be complete before federal reimbursement.
EVV: from April 1, 2026, quarterly compliance must stay above 75% where EVV applies. Whether 60D/61H CILA claims are covered is unverified, so confirm with DDD.
Certify to DDD that wage increases are passed through to direct care staff.

policies.title: Licensure, Certification and Provider Agreements
state_specifics: BALC license first (provisional up to 1 year for one site, up to 8 people), then IMPACT/DDD enrollment. A CILA serves 8 or fewer individuals.
Pass the BALC site visit within six months of first admission to convert to a permanent license. An unannounced visit occurs within the first year of the first admission.
The agency must be operational within 18 months or the application is treated as abandoned.
File the renewal application at least 120 days before expiry, after Department notice.
Notify BALC and DDD within 60 business days of any ownership change.

policies.title: Personal Funds and Property Management
state_specifics: CILA settings support individuals' control of their own personal resources.
Keep individuals' funds in separate accounts from agency funds, with a ledger, receipts and monthly reconciliation.
Charges for room and board need a written agreement. Verify the permitted amount with DDD or BALC.
Report suspected misuse as financial exploitation under GPR-05.

policies.title: Individual Rights and HCBS Settings Requirements
state_specifics: Provide and explain Rights of Individuals (IL 462-1201) at entry and annually.
Rights follow Chapter II of the Mental Health and DD Code. Seclusion is not permitted.
Individuals have the right to remain in the CILA unless they voluntarily withdraw or meet the termination criteria.
Individuals may use private physicians and professionals of their choice, documented in the plan.
Provider-owned or controlled sites meet 42 CFR 441.301(c)(4)(vi)(A)-(E).

policies.title: Rights Restrictions and Due Process
state_specifics: Any restriction is a documented modification in the Personal Plan, based on a specific assessed need.
The record shows less intrusive methods tried, a time limit, a data-based review, and informed consent from the individual or guardian.
The Human Rights Committee reviews restrictions affecting a specific individual at least every six months (GPR-02).
The individual and guardian are told how to appeal and who to contact (GAC, Equip for Equality, OIG, DHS).

policies.title: Informed Consent, Decision-Making Support and Sexual Health
state_specifics: Informed consent to participate in a CILA is documented in the record.
Informed consent includes consent to release of information. Use plain language and the individual's preferred communication mode.
Provider Support Team supports the individual's right to sexual health and freedom from sexual exploitation, including a decision-making capacity assessment for consent to sexual activity.
Where there is a guardian, the guardian's authority is documented. Guardian decisions never override the individual's rights beyond the court order.

policies.title: Nondiscrimination and Communication Access
state_specifics: Nondiscrimination categories follow 115.320(c)(4)(A) (see GPR-07).
Provide interpreters, translated materials and assistive communication supports at no cost.
Communal areas meet ADA accessibility standards.
Record each individual's preferred communication mode in the entry record.

policies.title: Privacy, Confidentiality and HIPAA
state_specifics: Illinois' Mental Health and DD Confidentiality Act (740 ILCS 110) and HIPAA both apply. Apply whichever is more protective.
CILA settings protect privacy, dignity and respect (115.200). Individuals have privacy in sleeping and bathing areas and control of their own mail and phone.
Authorized electronic monitoring follows 210 ILCS 165.
Provide a Notice of Privacy Practices. Breaches are investigated and reported under HIPAA.

policies.title: Person-Centered Planning, Personal Plan and Implementation Strategy
state_specifics: Provider signature page returns to the ISC within 10 calendar days of receiving the Personal Plan.
Develop the Implementation Strategy on Form IL462-4470 within 20 calendar days of the QIDP's dated signature. The individual and guardian sign it. The ISC does not sign or approve it.
Give the individual, guardian and ISC a copy of the strategy and every update.
The QIDP reviews the strategy at least monthly and documents the review.
The ISC has 30 calendar days after services begin to complete Discovery and develop the Personal Plan.

policies.title: Provider Support Team, Assessments and Requests for Additional Supports
state_specifics: The Provider Support Team includes a QIDP and a DSP, plus a nurse or other professionals as needed. It is available 24 hours.
Assessments inform the Personal Plan and Implementation Strategy. 115.225 text and the health-risk screening requirement should be pinned before finalizing.
Team requests for additional staff resources go to the Department, which responds no later than ten business days after receipt.
Need for non-base support hours is professionally reviewed at least annually and reported to the Department.

policies.title: Implementation of Supports and Daily Documentation
state_specifics: Staff carry out the Implementation Strategy outcomes and record daily activity, as the strategy specifies.
The QIDP signs and dates monthly progress documentation toward Personal Plan outcomes.
Provider support includes ADL help, assistive devices, crisis problem-solving and advocacy.
Services billed must match services in the Personal Plan.

policies.title: Community Integration and Employment Choice
state_specifics: CILA settings support integration and full community access.
The CILA rate excludes day programs, which are billed separately.
Document each person's choices about work, day program, activities and community access in the Personal Plan.
Describe the supports to help individuals take part in community supports.

policies.title: Transition, Discharge and Termination of Services
state_specifics: Individuals may remain in the CILA unless they voluntarily withdraw or meet the 115.215 termination criteria. 115.215 text was not retrieved, so pull it verbatim before finalizing this policy.
Involve the individual, guardian, ISC and Provider Support Team in any transition. Give written notice and a transition plan.
The agency stays responsible for affected individuals until they transition to another setting (see QA-02).
Return funds and property at discharge with a signed inventory.

policies.title: Medication Administration, Medical Services and Staff Certification
state_specifics: A licensed physician (MD/DO) is responsible for medical services, including prescribing, and examines the individual before psychotropics start.
AIMS screening is done at least every six months for individuals on psychotropic medications.
A physician reviews medications and sees the individual at least every six months, or more often if a psychiatrist requires.
Only staff who completed the Nurse-Trainer program under 59 Ill. Adm. Code 116 administer or supervise self-administration (TRN-05).
The agency certifies compliance with the Mental Health and DD Administrative Act and Part 116.

policies.title: Nursing Oversight and Health Care Coordination
state_specifics: The agency has an RN with a current unencumbered Illinois license who completes the DHS/DDD RN trainer webinars.
The RN trains and evaluates direct care staff on medications and reviews health records.
Coordinate physician, dental and specialist care with the Provider Support Team.
Staff help individuals access medication information and observe and report effects and side effects.

policies.title: Health Monitoring, Seizures, Choking Risk, Change of Condition and Emergency Medical Care
state_specifics: Staff are trained on how to react to psychiatric and medical emergencies, poison control and deaths (115.300).
A phone is operational and the poison control number is posted. Obtain consent to emergency medical services at entry.
Document individual seizure and choking risk plans in the record. Staff are trained on them.
Notify the guardian, RN and physician of a change of condition. Report any critical incident under CI-02.

policies.title: Emergency Preparedness and Fire Drills
state_specifics: Keep a disaster preparedness plan covering disasters and public health crises, reviewed annually.
Evacuation drills include actual evacuation to safe areas. Record corrective actions for drill or inspection deficiencies.
At least one approved fire extinguisher with an annual inspection tag. Red Cross-standard first aid kits are checked quarterly and restocked.
Fire and disaster training records are available at the site to DDD and BALC. New individuals are trained within 30 days of moving in.

policies.title: Infection Prevention and Control
state_specifics: Cover public health crises in the disaster plan (115.300).
Respite requires a physician statement of no contagious disease.
Standard precautions and hand hygiene. Bloodborne pathogens training and exposure control under OSHA.
Keep local and State health and sanitation inspection copies at the site.

policies.title: Food, Nutrition and Modified Diets
state_specifics: Dietary needs and modified diets are written in the Implementation Strategy, with physician or dietitian orders.
Individuals choose meals and have access to food, consistent with HCBS settings rules.
Choking-risk textures and aspiration precautions are posted for staff.
Any food restriction is a rights modification (RTS-02).

policies.title: Transportation and Vehicle Safety
state_specifics: Drivers hold a valid license. The agency checks driving records.
Confirm any BALC requirement for agency vehicles and insurance. No agency insurance minimum was located in Part 115.
Maintain vehicles and keep first aid kits and emergency contacts in them.
Wheelchair securement and seat-belt use are required. Accessible transportation is provided as the Personal Plan requires.

required_items.text: Policies and procedures of the agency
Organizational chart, staffing patterns, and staff qualifications for the agency

Governing body: each CILA provider owned or operated by any corporation, association, or unit of local government shall have a governing body in which is vested authority and responsibility for the organization, management, control, and operation of the CILA agency and all programs, services, facilities, and residences it administers.
Each CILA provider shall have provisions for obtaining input from individuals served, guardians and/or individual's representatives to the governing body.
Staffing: Mental health and developmental disabilities employees shall be licensed or certified as required by Illinois laws.
When paraprofessional, non-professional contractual workers or volunteers are used in direct services, they shall be supervised in the provision of services by professional employees.

A CILA provider shall not employ an individual (including contractual workers, volunteers, or practitioners who have the responsibility of caring for individuals) in any capacity, until the provider has conducted these registry checks: (A) DPH Health Care Worker Registry; (B) DCFS State Central Register/CANTS; (C) Illinois Sex Offender Registry; (D) HFS Sanctions List (HFS OIG).

A CILA provider shall not employ an individual in any capacity until it has inquired of and received the results from the applicable registry or list. Inquiries shall not occur more than 30 calendar days prior to the first day of employment.

If the DPH, DCFS, or Illinois Sex Offender registries show a finding of physical or sexual abuse or egregious neglect, a substantiated case of child abuse or neglect, a sex offense, or a disqualifying criminal conviction with no waiver, the provider shall not employ that person in any capacity. If the HFS Sanctions List shows the person has been excluded from the Illinois Medical Assistance Program, the provider shall confirm that person's status with the HFS OIG.

CILA providers shall make annual inquiries to the DPH, DCFS, and Illinois Sex Offender registries and the HFS Sanctions List for each current employee, volunteer, contractual worker, subcontractor, or licensed practitioner. A person whose name has been placed on the registry or list must be terminated. The provider must establish a schedule that results in completion of checks every full year (365 calendar days), by (A) repeating the check on the anniversary of hiring, (B) repeating it when the annual performance evaluation is due, or (C) creating a specific schedule of checks.
The CILA provider must comply with the Health Care Worker Background Check Act [225 ILCS 46]. A CILA provider shall not knowingly hire or retain any person outside of the provisions of the Act.

A person listed on the Health Care Worker Registry may request a waiver of the prohibition against employment by completing an application on a form prescribed by DPH in accordance with the Health Care Worker Background Check Act.
A waiver of an indication on the CANTS Register may be requested by completing an application per the guidelines issued and published by the Department.
Recordkeeping: Cumulative case records including a Personal Plan and Implementation Strategy shall be maintained for each individual.

Behavior management and human rights review: Each CILA agency is required to have a Human Rights Committee that will establish or ensure a process for the periodic review of human rights issues involved in the individual's services and supports. A program that uses behavioral interventions as specified in Section 115.214 shall also establish a Behavior Management Committee. Each Committee must have at least five members, and members shall not be shared between committees except a physician, APRN, registered professional nurse, or nurse practitioner/physician assistant.

The Human Rights Committee shall: (i) review at least annually the CILA provider policies, procedures and practices which have the potential to restrict the rights of individuals; (ii) review at least every six months practices which restrict a specific individual's rights; (iii) inform the CILA agency of any complaints involving an individual's rights, deficiencies, and any corrective actions; (iv) ensure that individuals, guardians, and natural supports as desired are included in meetings about their services and supports; (v) maintain minutes, including attendance and a record of decisions made per individual, with justification and intended outcomes. When restrictive interventions are approved, the minutes must include the next review date.

The Human Rights Committee shall include: (i) at least 5 members; (ii) at least one person receiving services from the agency and/or the individual's family member or guardian; (iii) at least one-third of the members who are not former employees of the CILA provider, individuals or guardians of individuals formerly served by the provider, a vendor providing products or services to the provider, or employees from other CILA providers or DD programs.

A Behavior Management Committee shall: (i) approve behavior interventions prior to implementation and review them at least every six months; (ii) review all behavior strategies at least annually and determine if a rights restriction exists. Plans with a rights restriction must also be reviewed by the Human Rights Committee; (iii) maintain minutes, including attendance and a record of decisions made; (iv) seek input from individuals, guardians, and natural supports as desired.

A Behavior Management Committee shall be comprised as follows: (i) members shall include persons qualified to evaluate the appropriateness of proposed behavior management interventions; (ii) when drugs to manage behavior are used, a licensed professional qualified to evaluate their use shall be a member; (iii) at least one member shall be from outside the CILA agency.

Abuse, neglect, and exploitation: Each CILA agency shall have and use a process for reporting and handling instances of abuse, neglect, and exploitation in accordance with applicable standards, regulations and laws. It shall include notification of the individual allegedly abused, neglected, or exploited and their guardian or parent of the allegation within 24 hours after receiving the allegation.

In addition to abuse, neglect, and exploitation, each CILA agency shall have and use a process for reporting and handling complaints regarding individual rights. The agency shall share a copy of the Rights of Individuals form [IL 462-1201] with the individual and/or guardian when an individual enters the CILA program (see Section 115.250(a)).

Admission requirements: CILA agencies shall not discriminate in the admission to and provision of needed services on the basis of race, color, sex, religion (creed), gender identity, gender expression, age, national origin (ancestry), ethnicity, disability, marital status, sexual orientation or military status in any of their activities or operations.
Admission policies and procedures shall be set forth in writing and be available for review.

Compliance with life safety standards and requirements: All program facilities shall be in compliance with applicable State licensure requirements and local ordinances with regard to fire, building, zoning, sanitation, health, and safety requirements.

Visits to programs: The CILA agency shall ensure that Department-authorized individual protection and advocacy interest groups shall be permitted, with the consent of the individual or guardian, to visit provider-owned or controlled living arrangements.

Remote Monitoring and Supports: CILA agencies may provide remote monitoring and support services pursuant to 305 ILCS 5/12-21.21, as determined by DDD. Remote supports and services must be based on an assessment which shall, at a minimum, identify risks important in considering whether remote monitoring and supports are appropriate for the individual. (Applies only if the agency offers this service.)

Training: Direct service professionals and any other persons (paraprofessional, contractual workers, or volunteers) with responsibility for direct care shall demonstrate competence in the training areas listed in (d)(1)(A) through (M) as part of an orientation program. Anyone without previous experience in direct service shall receive training and demonstrate competence prior to unsupervised responsibility for direct service unless trained employees are on site and available for on-the-job training. Training and competence must be documented in employee records.
Cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR), back blows/abdominal thrusts, and first aid;

Concepts of habilitation and rehabilitation including behavior intervention and management, age appropriateness and psycho-social rehabilitation depending on the needs of the individuals served or to be served;
Safety and disaster procedures; public health emergencies; and fire procedures and the use of fire equipment such as a fire extinguisher;
Abuse, neglect, exploitation, coercion and critical incident prevention, handling and reporting to the DHS OIG (pursuant to 59 Ill. Adm. Code 50);
Individual rights in accordance with Section 115.250 and maintaining confidentiality in accordance with the Mental Health and Developmental Disabilities Confidentiality Act [740 ILCS 100];
The purpose and content of the Personal Plan pursuant to 42 CFR 441.301(c)(2);
Development and implementation of an Implementation Strategy;

The type, dosage, characteristics, effects, and side effects of medications prescribed for individuals. The CILA agency shall ensure that there is sufficient training in this area to provide coverage during expected and unexpected absences of caregivers by others who have been determined competent;
Observation, using the AIMS (Abnormal Involuntary Movement Skills), of involuntary muscular movement, which may be indicative of tardive dyskinesia;
Documentation and recordkeeping requirements with reference to the Personal Plan and Implementation Strategy;

Other training which relates specifically to the type of disability or treatment and intervention techniques being used specific to individuals living in CILAs, geared toward assisting employees to execute outcomes stated in the Personal Plans and Implementation Strategies;

The techniques associated with monitoring and regulating hot water temperatures prior to and during an individual's use to ensure safe hand-washing, hair-washing, bathing, and showering procedures. Water temperatures should be between 100 and 110 degrees to ensure safety; and

In CILA programs for individuals with developmental disabilities, all unlicensed, direct care employees, prior to assuming responsibility for supervising self-administration of medication or for administering medications, shall meet criteria in 59 Ill. Adm. Code 116.40(c), including successful completion of a Department-approved training program provided by a CILA agency Nurse-Trainer. Authorized direct care staff shall be re-evaluated by a Nurse-Trainer at least annually or more frequently at the discretion of the registered professional nurse. Any retraining shall be to the extent necessary to ensure competency (see 59 Ill. Adm. Code 116.40).

After completion of training specified in subsection (d)(1), each direct service employee shall participate in ongoing employee development activities as outlined in the CILA agency's employee development plan.
All training shall be documented and shall be readily available for review by BALC and DDD.

The CILA agency shall implement a written training plan which lists training to be offered to meet the requirements of this Part, the methods used for completion of any required training, and the process used to determine competency.

Volunteer training: The CILA agency shall provide an orientation and training program for volunteers specific to volunteer duties and shall provide supervision as necessary. Volunteers with responsibility for care of individuals served must complete and demonstrate competency in the training areas specified in subsection (d).

Quality assurance: There shall be a written quality assurance plan and ongoing activities designed to review and evaluate services to individuals and operation of programs and to resolve identified problems.

The CILA agency's quality assurance program shall be the basis for determining under its license that individuals are receiving appropriate community-based services consistent with their Personal Plans and Implementation Strategies and that all programs and services are supervised by the agency and comply with this Part. (A) If a certified CILA does not continue to meet standards, the agency shall correct deficiencies within 30 days. (B) If deficiencies cannot be corrected within 30 days, the agency shall withdraw certification of the CILA program in question and notify the Department, and remains responsible for the affected individuals until they have transitioned to other settings.

Critical incidents: The CILA agency shall have written policies and procedures for handling, investigating, reporting, tracking, and analyzing critical incidents through the agency's management structure, up to and including the authorized CILA agency representative. The agency shall ensure that employees demonstrate their knowledge of, and follow, such policies and procedures.
Within 24 hours of occurrence the CILA agency shall report any incident which is subject to the Criminal Code of 2012 [720 ILCS 5] to the local law enforcement agencies.

The CILA agency shall ensure that suspected instances of abuse, neglect or exploitation against individuals in programs licensed by the Department are reported to the Office of Inspector General within four hours of discovery.

Incidents other than those required to be reported to the Office of Inspector General shall be electronically reported to DDD through its Critical Incident Reporting and Analysis System (CIRAS). Incidents to be reported are specified in Section 115.120 under Critical Incidents.
Individuals' records: The CILA agency shall ensure the confidentiality of individuals' records in accordance with the Act and shall ensure safekeeping of all records against loss or destruction.

The CILA agency shall maintain a chronological record for each individual, accessible at the program site. (A) Each entry shall be legible, dated and authenticated by the signature and title of the person making the entry. (B) Corrections shall be initialed and made so the original incorrect entry stays legible. (C) When symbols or abbreviations are used, the agency shall provide a legend, standardized throughout the agency.

On an individual's entry into the CILA agency, the following shall be obtained, recorded, and updated as necessary: (A) identifying information; (B) court-appointed guardianship order, if applicable; (C) name, address and telephone number of the legal guardian or emergency contact; (D) language spoken or understood, including preferred mode of communication; (E) prescribed medications, reactions and side effects, allergies; (F) physical and dental examinations and medical history; (G) consent to receive emergency medical services; (H) copies of the authorization for release of information.

The following shall be entered in the individual's record during the period of service: (A) written informed consent by the individual or guardian to participate in a CILA; (B) prior service history; (C) Personal Plan and Implementation Strategy (Section 115.230); (D) assessments and reassessments (Section 115.225); (E) documentation of approval to use special procedures and the results of their use; (F) monthly documentation of progress towards Personal Plan outcomes, signed and dated by the QIDP.

Electronic signature or computer-generated signature codes are acceptable as authentication of record content. (A) The agency must adopt a policy that permits authentication by electronic or computer-generated signature. (B) The policy shall include safeguards to ensure confidentiality of the codes: (i) unique identifier per user generated through a confidential access code; (ii) written certification that each identifier is kept strictly confidential, with a commitment to terminate use of a misused identifier; (iii) written user certification that the user is the only person with access to the identifier; (iv) periodic monitoring of identifier use with corrective action, with the monitoring process described in the policy. (C) A verification process shall ensure the content of authenticated entries is accurate: (i) required completion of designated fields, with corrections made by separate subsequent authenticated entries; (ii) opportunity for the user to verify the document and signature; (iii) periodic sampling of system-generated records. (D) Each report generated by a user must be separately authenticated.
Financial and operational requirements: Agencies licensed to provide CILA services shall comply with Department rules regulating their contractual and financial relationship with the Department.

official.notes: No public BALC policy checklist or form was found. BALC releases the CILA licensure application only after New Provider Orientation, so it could not be reviewed. The items above come from the rule sections that list the written policies and plans a CILA agency must have, mainly 115.320, with 115.410(a)(3)(D)-(E) showing the application requests agency policies and procedures plus an organizational chart, staffing patterns and staff qualifications. Submission sequence from the DHS 'Steps for CILA' page: (1) attend New Provider Orientation; (2) request the application from BALC (DHS.BALC@illinois.gov, 312-814-5310); (3) submit the application with the $200 nonrefundable fee and fingerprint background checks; (4) pass the initial BALC interview; (5) submit policies and procedures, a projected two-year budget, sample case files and sample implementation strategies (budget and case files are not policy content, so they are excluded here); (6) if the policies are approved, receive a provisional license. BALC works with the applicant on revisions. If the interview or the policies fail, the applicant cannot reapply for one calendar year. After a first admission, BALC does a site visit within six months and, if the agency passes, issues a 3-year permanent license. The reviewer expects the manual to track the 115.320 lettering. Other Part 115 sections also require written content and should be cross-referenced in the manual. These were not fetched in full because ilga.gov blocked some pages: 115.200 (principles, critical incidents), 115.214 (behavioral interventions), 115.225 (assessments), 115.230 (Personal Plan and Implementation Strategy), 115.240 (medical services and medications), 115.250 (individual rights and confidentiality, the Rights of Individuals form IL 462-1201), 115.300 (environmental management, including life safety and a written policy on food dates), 115.310 (geographic location), and the termination criteria section. DSP and QIDP training programs go separately to DDD's Bureau of Quality Management for approval after enrollment, and the implementation strategy must be approved before billing. Confirm the current BALC packet and checklist directly with BALC.
